author_or_org: James C. Davis, Paschal C. Amusuo, Tanmay Singla, Berk Çakar, Kirsten A. Davis

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The paper frames the shift as moving software engineering from scarce implementation effort to abundant, low-cost code production, making organization of architectures, tools, evidence, and feedback loops the central problem.
claims.quote: Generative AI is shifting software engineering from a practice organized around scarce implementation effort toward one organized around abundant, low-cost code production. This shift changes the central engineering problem: not whether AI can generate useful code, but how engineers organize architectures, tools, evidence, and feedback loops so that AI-mediated development remains inspectable, correctable, and maintainable.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: In a 12-week first-person case study, one expert engineer used frontier AI coding agents to build a document accessibility remediation system, with an empirical record of 88 field notes, 420 KLOC of production code, and 1.16 MLOC of tests, lints, documentation, and agent tooling.
claims.quote: We study this problem through a first-person case study: a 12-week development effort in which a single expert software engineer used frontier AI coding agents to build a document accessibility remediation system. The empirical record comprises 88 contemporaneous field notes, 420 KLOC of production code, and 1.16 MLOC of tests, lints, supporting documentation, and agent tooling.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The evidence base is a single-expert first-person case study over 12 weeks, so it does not directly measure team shape, roles, or organization-level effects.
claims.quote: We study this problem through a first-person case study: a 12-week development effort in which a single expert software engineer used frontier AI coding agents to build a document accessibility remediation system.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The paper develops a candidate middle-range theory of governance conversion, a process model for how high-velocity agentic implementation becomes governable.
claims.quote: From this record, we develop a candidate middle-range theory of governance conversion, expressed as a process model explaining how high-velocity agentic implementation becomes governable.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The model claims that engineering judgment sustains agentic velocity by converting recurring structural failure classes into durable governance mechanisms.
claims.quote: The model explains how agentic implementation velocity surfaces recurring structural failure classes, and how engineering judgment sustains velocity by converting those failures into durable governance mechanisms.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The governance-conversion model says controls are discovered from failures visible only during agentic work, contrasting with governance models that derive controls from known obligations.
claims.quote: In contrast to existing governance models that derive controls from known obligations, governance conversion explains how controls are discovered from failures that become visible only during agentic work.
